changes.headline: Two ships sink near Hormuz; attack tempo at wartime highs; crude fades anyway
changes.dek: GFS Pride sunk (struck Oct 13, confirmed Oct 14 by Singapore MPA, all 21 crew safe); GFS Giselle struck Oct 14, hull damaged, anchored safely (22 crew safe); Cape Dao sank as delayed outcome of Sep 23 strike (1 seafarer died then); at least 10 vessels attacked since Sunday, 23 since Oct 1; Houthis threaten Saudi oil facilities by name; overnight WTI Nov26 $94.11 (-$0.98) / Brent Dec26 $104.42 (-$1.64) after Wed settles WTI $95.09 / Brent $106.06. Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority confirmed Wednesday that GFS Pride (2,824 TEU), struck Tuesday in the Strait of Hormuz, caught fire and sank; all 21 crew evacuated safely. GFS Giselle was struck Wednesday, took hull damage, and reached a safe anchorage with all 22 crew safe. Cape Dao sank as the delayed outcome of a Sep 23 strike. Vanguard/IMO/UKMTO data show at least 10 vessels attacked since Sunday (six Sunday, four Tuesday) and 23 attacks since Oct 1; the IMO recorded 106 confirmed incidents and 24 seafarer fatalities as of Oct 13. The Houthis threatened further strikes on Saudi oil facilities and airports Wednesday, naming Aramco facilities in Dhahran and a Riyadh refinery; Aramco operations continued normally. Overnight crude fell more than $1 despite the sinkings.
changes.balance_read: Sinkings raise war-risk and freight but have not removed export barrels: the IEA puts Gulf crude exports at about 75 percent of prewar in September, and Washington is floating a shadow-fleet easing aimed at shipping costs. Bulls hold tempo and named process targets; bears hold the export recovery and a possible freight policy lever. What changes the read is loadings falling or a Saudi process hit, not incident counts alone.
changes.publishers: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore, Oct 14, 2026; Reuters, Oct 15, 2026; Vanguard/IMO/UKMTO via AFP, Oct 15, 2026; IEA Oil Market Report, Oct 14, 2026

changes.headline: IEA cuts demand, reports on-land stocks lowest since 2016; crack eases to $102.05; ceasefire restraint ends
changes.dek: IEA Oct report: 2026 demand 102.4 Mb/d (-2.6), diesel 25% of the drop, 2027 recovery cut to +2.0; September supply 102.3 Mb/d (+2.5 m/m); observed stocks below 7.8 billion, -509 Mbbl vs end-February, on-land lowest since at least 2016; no diesel restocking until 2H 2027. Diesel crack $102.05, ninth day above $100, down about $10. Kremlin: ceasefire terms not established. Zelenskiy: refinery strikes resume. No Russian diesel loading.. The IEA October report (Oct 14) cut 2026 demand to 102.4 Mb/d (down 2.6 Mb/d), with diesel a quarter of the decline, and cut the 2027 recovery to +2.0 Mb/d, leaving 2027 demand 620 kb/d below 2025. September supply rose 2.5 Mb/d to 102.3 Mb/d and Gulf crude exports reached about 75 percent of prewar. Observed stocks fell 10 Mbbl in September to below 7.8 billion barrels, 509 Mbbl below end-February, with on-land stocks the lowest since at least 2016; diesel exports were about 700 kb/d below a year earlier and no meaningful restocking is seen until 2H 2027. The diesel crack eased to $102.05 (ninth straight day above $100; maximum $117.92 Sep 16); the 3-2-1 reads $57.75. The Kremlin said Wednesday the energy ceasefire terms have not been established; Novak confirmed Russia-US diesel contract negotiations; Zelenskiy told the FT Ukraine will resume refinery strikes. No cargo has loaded.
changes.balance_read: Demand destruction at the margin and scarcity in the stock is the configuration where flat price fades and cracks stay bid: the crack gave back about $10 on talk and positioning but the physical supports (record-low US diesel stocks, no restocking until 2H 2027, zero loadings) are intact. Zelenskiy's resumption pushes the first loading further out if executed.
changes.publishers: IEA Oil Market Report, Oct 14, 2026; validated crack history, refreshed Oct 15, 2026; Reuters, Oct 14, 2026; Financial Times via Reuters, Oct 15, 2026

changes.headline: WCS December widens to -$26.25; EIA delayed to today against an 11.12 Mbbl API draw
changes.dek: WCS Dec26 -$26.25 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 14), down $0.70 on 110 lots, widest tenor; SYN Nov26 +$7.45; C5 Dec26 +$5.25, up $0.25 on 290 lots; ARV-TMW December +$9.05. EIA week ending Oct 9 prints today (Thursday, delayed); API preview crude -11.12 Mbbl, distillate -1.5, Cushing +1.82; SPR flat at 283 Mbbl. AESO Oct 15: all SAGD cogen at full capability.. Canadian diffs (ICE, Oct 14): TMW Nov26 -$24.91 (zero volume) and Dec26 -$26.25, down $0.70 on 110 lots, still the widest tenor; Jan27 -$25.35. ARV Dec26 -$17.20; ARV-TMW December +$9.05, the implied export arb, steady. SYN Nov26 +$7.45 (+$0.43) ahead of the Syncrude coker return wrapping Oct 16. C5 Dec26 +$5.25, up $0.25 on 290 lots, a partial bounce after Tuesday's $1.00 markdown. MSW Nov26 -$0.54 (+$0.42); UHC Dec26 +$2.35 unchanged. The EIA report for the week ending Oct 9 did not print Wednesday and is scheduled today; API preview showed crude down 11.12 Mbbl, gasoline up 1.1, distillate down 1.5, Cushing up 1.82, with the SPR flat at 283 Mbbl. Last confirmed EIA row (week ending Oct 2): crude excluding SPR 424.134 Mbbl, distillate 105.138 Mbbl, PADD 2 crude 106.981 Mbbl, utilization 92.7 percent. AESO Oct 15, 01:39 MDT: all monitored SAGD cogen units at full maximum capability, grid Normal.
changes.balance_read: December WCS is pricing the seasonal wide ahead of the November apportionment notice (about Oct 19), which remains the decision print for the binding-from-November base case. SYN firmness into tomorrow's Syncrude return is the lights tell; C5's partial bounce says Tuesday's markdown was aggressive, not yet reversed. Today's EIA is storm accounting except for PADD 2.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 14, 2026; API weekly data via OilPrice, Oct 14, 2026; EIA WPSR week ending Oct 2, released Oct 7, 2026; AESO CSD, Oct 15, 2026

flags.title: Hormuz sinkings: tempo at wartime highs, exports not yet hit
flags.detail: GFS Pride has sunk and GFS Giselle was damaged, with at least 10 attacks since Sunday and 23 since Oct 1. Gulf crude exports were at about 75 percent of prewar in September (IEA). The risk is loadings falling or a Saudi process asset being hit; incident counts alone have not removed barrels. Trigger: Gulf export loadings fall materially, or a strike hits Saudi process, pipeline or export assets

flags.title: Ceasefire restraint over; loadings still zero; crack $102.05
flags.detail: The Kremlin says no ceasefire terms were established, Zelenskiy says refinery strikes resume, and Russia-US diesel contract talks continue as commerce. No Russian diesel cargo has loaded. The crack is nine days above $100 at $102.05, down about $10 from Wednesday. Trigger: A Russian diesel cargo loads, or Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries resume in fact

flags.title: SPR 40 Mbbl award still pending, nine days after bids
flags.detail: No DOE award announcement as of early Thursday, nine days after the Oct 6 bid deadline. The award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery when it lands. Separately, Washington is considering easing sanctions on shadow-fleet vessels for legal cargoes, which would pressure freight if enacted. Trigger: DOE announces the exchange award, or a shadow-fleet easing instrument is published

forward_calendar.what: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (w/e Oct 9, delayed)
forward_calendar.detail: Prints Thursday after a Wednesday delay. API preview was crude -11.12 Mbbl against a Street expectation near flat; the week is the Isaias shut-in week, so read PADD 2 and the restart lines, not the production headline.
Bids went in Oct 6 (11:00 a.m. CT); a clean award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery. No award announced nine days later.

SCO supply returns into late October, softening SYN against WCS. SYN Nov26 firmed to +$7.45 on Oct 14, ahead of the return. Suncor Edmonton/Base Plant fall work ended Oct 13 and the Horizon upgrader turnaround implies completion about Oct 12 to 13.

forward_calendar.what: Riyadh King Khalid airport closure scheduled to end
forward_calendar.detail: GACA has closed the airport to 21:00 GMT Oct 17 after the Houthi strikes. Whether it reopens on schedule is a read on Saudi air-defence confidence after the Dhahran Aramco HQ strike and renewed Houthi threats against airports.
Decides whether the binding-from-November base case is right; December TMW is already pricing the seasonal wide (-$26.25, ICE settle Oct 14).
Next scheduled OPEC+ meeting; quotas are not the constraint, actual supply is.
